source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
A substantial part of this thesis (roughly a third of its length) consists of architectural site plans and building elevation drawings for the proposed plantation's support infrastructure rather than crop-growing technique. It covers: an overall site layout plan showing the office building, staff housing rooms, a well, a water tank, a fence line along the road frontage, and a seed/produce storage warehouse; detailed floor plans and elevations for two office building designs (referred to as a main office-cum-warehouse-viewing building and a second smaller office type labeled 'K-K'); a design for an office/storage building; worker housing block layout; fence design; water tank design; and warehouse (produce/seed storage) building layout and elevation, including a dedicated seed-storage hangar design.

This content is architectural/construction planning specific to this one proposed farm site rather than general coconut-growing knowledge, so it is summarized here rather than reproduced drawing-by-drawing; the substantive farming technique and business-economics content of the thesis is captured in the other topic files from this source.
